en.title: Does separating PSA decline and regrowth improve early prediction?
en.summary: A public clinical PSA dataset used to compare landmark prediction, uncertainty calibration and decline/regrowth identifiability against simple benchmarks.
key_findings: In 400 patients from a public PSA dataset, a decline–regrowth hierarchical model predicted the next 12 weeks of PSA better than linear or single-decay models at every landmark (MAE 0.429 vs 0.543–0.565 at 6 weeks).
Its advantage over simply carrying the last PSA value forward was uncertain at 6 and 12 weeks, and at 24 weeks the last value was more accurate (MAE 0.249 vs 0.327).
The regrowth rate was weakly identified, with its population mean at the lower bound at every landmark, so no minimum observation period for a regrowth-based decision can be set from these data.
en.seo_title: Does separating PSA decline and regrowth improve prediction?

ja.title: 早期PSAの低下と再上昇を分ければ予測は良くなるか
ja.summary: 公開PSA400人で低下・再上昇の階層モデルを直近値予測と比較し、早期予測誤差、再上昇速度の同定、治療継続者への選択を分けて検討する。
ja.seo_title: 早期PSA予測と再上昇速度の同定
